desc:
A maze is an integer matrix maze in which 0 is an open cell and 1 is a wall. The top-left cell and the bottom-right cell are always open (they are the same cell when the maze has a single cell).

A route starts at the top-left cell and moves one step at a time to the open cell directly above, below, left or right. A route may not visit any cell twice, and it ends the first time it reaches the bottom-right cell. Return the number of different routes. Two routes are different when they visit their cells in a different order.

For example, an open 2 x 2 maze has 2 routes (right then down, or down then right), and an open 3 x 3 maze has 12 routes, because routes may also wander, for example through the cells (0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0), (2,0), (2,1), (2,2), as long as they never step on a used cell.
constraints: maze[0][0] = 0 and the bottom-right cell is 0
hints: A route is a sequence of cells, so it can be built one cell at a time. Count how many ways each partial route can be finished.

Keep a visited grid. From the current cell try each of the 4 neighbours that is inside the maze, open and not visited, recurse, and then mark the neighbour as unvisited again so that other routes may use it.
When the recursion arrives at the bottom-right cell it has found one complete route: return 1 and do not continue past that cell. The answer is the sum over all choices.
editorial: This is plain backtracking with undo. go(r, c) returns the number of ways to finish a route that currently stands on (r, c). At the target it returns 1. Otherwise it marks the cell visited, adds up go over the neighbours that are open and unvisited, and finally unmarks the cell, so that a different route can pass through it later.

The number of routes can be much larger than the number of cells (an open 5 x 5 maze already has 8,512), and the search enumerates every route, so the running time grows with the answer. The size limit of 30 cells keeps the answer small enough for that. A simple speed-up is to stop a branch when the target is no longer reachable from the current cell, but it is not needed here.
